description: The paper's feature generation block, Eqs. (8)-(16), placed between the third and fourth ResNet blocks, with L_MSE (Eq. S4) added to the objective. Every cell carries v8.1's R-aug-t2 directed augmentation, so the factor under test is the generation block alone; R-aug-t2 itself supplies the reference row.

feature_generation.position: between the third and fourth ResNet block, Section 2.4: 'Rs(.) means the first three convolutional layers; the remaining part is recorded as Rf(.)'
feature_generation.decomposition: MaxPool(kernel 2, stride 2) then nearest-neighbour upsample gives z^H; z^L = z - z^H. Eqs. (8)-(9).
feature_generation.restyled_part: the residual z^L, per Eq. (15) z~ = z^H + z~^L. The paper calls the residual the low-frequency component, which reads correctly if the frequency meant is temporal: the residual carries the environment and the slow drift.
feature_generation.style_axis_note: Eqs. (10)-(11) sum over both the channel and the length axis, giving one scalar per sample; the sentence after says the result lives in R^{BxCH}, which is the shape of z^L itself and would make the restyle an identity. Neither is AdaIN's per-channel convention. Measured against the real target drift at this depth the three readings explain 1.2%, 15.3% and 30.1% of it, so per-position was taken. It corresponds approximately to per-sensor: position 8(s-1)+k came from sensor s's statistic k, smeared by a receptive field of plus or minus six.
feature_generation.batch_meaning: the training minibatch. The paper says only 'Bs is the number of batches of z_s', and z_s is the current minibatch's feature tensor, so Bs is its batch dimension. Measured, the style spread across a minibatch's samples is 1.40x the real target drift in the same space; the alternative of splitting Batch 1 by its two acquisition blocks gives 1.27x with a direction anti-correlated to the real drift (cosine -0.692), so it offers nothing and was dropped.
feature_generation.negative_scale: Eq. (14) draws delta' from an ordinary Gaussian, which can return a negative scale. This follows the paper rather than truncating, and records the fraction of negative draws in each run's history.
feature_generation.inference: never applied. Fig. 2: 'during forecasting, the program separates the data manipulation block from the prediction process', so src.evaluate runs the plain five-block backbone and every frozen checkpoint is scored without the block.

loss.equation: Eq. (4): min(L_ce + lambda_MSE L_MSE + lambda_con L_con). L_con is not implemented yet, so lambda_con is zero in every cell.
loss.L_MSE: Eq. (S4): the mean over samples of the summed squared difference between the two branches' softmax probabilities. The class axis carries no 1/C in the printed formula, so the six squared differences are summed; F.mse_loss's default reduction would be six times smaller and is exactly lambda_MSE/6 of this.
loss.lambda_mse_note: Eq. (4) calls lambda_MSE 'a weighting factor that belongs to [0,1]' and neither the paper nor the supplement gives a value. 0.5 is the declared default; R-gen-m10 runs 1.0 to measure the sensitivity.
loss.ce_branches: Eq. (S2) writes L_ce over Phi alone, so the generated branch reaches the objective only through L_MSE. The algorithm box's line 6, 'Compute the output of network out = FC(Zs), out = FC(Zs) and calculate Ll2 and Lce', reads as both branches. R-gen takes the first reading, R-gen-ce2 the second, averaging the two branches so the term keeps its scale.

confounds.inherited_target_informed_choices: Every cell carries R-aug-t2, whose direction and displacement were both chosen against target data. v9.0 therefore reports an upper bound in the same sense v8.1 did; the source-only settled number remains R-fig-logps at 0.5556.
confounds.style_axis_choice: The per-position reading was chosen by measuring how much of the real target drift each reading spans, which used target data. The choice is target-informed and the run reports it as such.
confounds.gradient_steps: The generation cells run two forward passes through Rf and the head per minibatch but take the same number of optimizer steps as R-aug-t2, so step count is matched and wall-clock is not.

paper_reference.note: CDWC is CDCNN without contrastive learning, so it is the closest published counterpart to a cell with augmentation and feature generation but no L_con. The paper's step from ResNet to CDWC is +0.036.

prediction.basis: The per-position style displacement a minibatch supplies is 1.40x the real target drift at block 3, but the block reaches only the 30.1% of that drift the style axes span; the backbone already suppresses 7.5% of the input drift, and augmentation made that fraction worse rather than better.
prediction.expectation: A gain of the paper's order (+0.036 from ResNet to CDWC) is the optimistic case. The realistic case is a gain under the separability threshold, because the block moves a component of the drift the backbone was not removing anyway. R-gen-ce2 should not differ much from R-gen: averaging L_ce over the two branches changes the term's target set but not its scale.
prediction.falsifier: If R-gen-m10 and R-gen differ by more than R-gen differs from R-aug-t2, the result is a lambda_MSE effect rather than a feature generation effect and the block's contribution is not established.

pre_run_measurement.when: before the v9.0 launch, on the frozen R-aug-t2 lr0.0003 seed1042 checkpoint of run 20260923T045843638020Z_displacement_full. Batch 1 only; no target file was opened.
pre_run_measurement.question: does the block perturb anything, and by how much against a real drift?

reference_scale.what: Batch 1's own first-to-second acquisition block centroid offset at z_f, relative to the mean feature norm

pre_run_measurement.reading: The per-position restyle moves z_f by 0.0448, which sits inside the 0.047 to 0.105 range a real two-month acquisition drift moves it. The block is doing work of the right magnitude, and it is the largest of the three style axes here as it was on the drift-span measurement. Negative delta draws, which Eq. (14) permits, occur at 0.0 under the per-position and scalar readings and 0.015 under per-channel, so following the paper rather than truncating costs nothing at this depth.
pre_run_measurement.consequence_for_the_loss: L_MSE lands near 0.004 in the 3-epoch CPU smoke, about 0.9 % of the total loss, because a 0.11 relative change to a near-one-hot softmax is small once squared and summed. With ce_on_generated false the generated branch reaches the objective only through that term, so R-gen gives the block a small gradient weight by construction. R-gen-m10 doubles it to the ceiling Eq. (4) allows; R-gen-ce2 is the cell where the generated branch enters at full weight. No cell goes outside the paper's declared lambda range of [0,1].
